response.passage: Atoms are the fundamental building blocks of all matter, yet they are mostly empty space rather than solid spheres. When atoms combine to form molecules, they do so in fixed, definite proportions by mass, regardless of the source or method of preparation of the substance. For instance, water molecules always contain hydrogen and oxygen in a constant ratio, whether obtained from a river or a laboratory. During chemical reactions, the total mass of the reactants remains equal to the total mass of the products, even if a gas is released, provided the reaction occurs in a closed system. To quantify these substances, we use the mole concept. One mole of any substance contains 6.022 x 10^23 particles, and its mass in grams is numerically equal to its molar mass. Importantly, molar mass represents the mass of one mole of particles, not the mass of a single atom or molecule. Furthermore, ions are formed when atoms lose or gain electrons, not protons, to achieve stability. Understanding these principles allows us to predict how matter behaves and transforms during various chemical processes.
response.summary: Atoms are mostly empty space and combine in fixed ratios to form molecules. Chemical reactions conserve mass, and the mole concept helps us relate the mass of substances to the number of particles they contain.
